findings.title: Findings converge on the inline Phase 4 investigation (D1-A) and what it produces per finding
findings.why_it_matters: Five findings from both critics all land on the new Phase 4. The ledger defines it only as "the main session, inline" with a prose instruction to prove or drop. It has no defined output per finding, no input from reviewers, no bound, no progress signal, and no record. Each finding proposes its own local patch: a required Proof line (3), a reviewer falsifier hand-off (4), a check cap, queue message, or budget (5), an entry rule for open questions (6), and persisted verdict files (7). Some of these patches conflict. Finding 5's budget option sends overflow to open questions as `not investigated: budget`, and Finding 6 calls exactly that item a defect. Should the investigation step be designed as a whole (what it takes in, what it emits per finding, what bounds it, what the user sees) rather than collecting five separate rules? Re-evaluation is open-ended. It may also conclude that D1-A as ratified holds once the other questions are answered, or that some of these failure modes are limitations to accept.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the inline Phase 4 investigation before addressing Findings 3–7 individually. Open questions it must answer: what each finding's investigation must produce and where that is recorded; whether reviewers or the main session run the first-pass check; what bounds the phase and what happens to findings past the bound; what the user sees while it runs and whether they can prune it; whether D1-A still holds once those are settled.
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the inline Phase 4 investigation before addressing Findings 3–7 individually
findings.choice_reason: re-evaluate is fine, but don't go too crazy defining the skill; a small prompt on Opus that asks it to dig in works well

findings.title: Findings converge on the report → draft → post presentation sequence (Phases 5–7)
findings.why_it_matters: The design adds two report sections (open questions from D3, tracker candidates from D6), a new label (D5), a routing call (D6), and full draft bodies before the post gate. It keeps today's Phase 5 report → automatic Phase 6 drafts → three-option Phase 7 gate unchanged. Five findings each patch that sequence locally. One merges the report into the drafts (8). One adds dispositions for open questions to the gate (9). One adds a gate between report and drafting (10). Two show the label and routing reason inline (11, 12). Findings 8 and 10 pull in opposite directions: 8 shows drafts as the report, while 10 holds drafting until the user has shaped the set. Should the post-investigation sequence (what the user reads, in what order, and which gates exist) be redesigned as one flow?
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the report → draft → post sequence before addressing Findings 8–12 individually. Open questions it must answer: how many views the user reads between the report and posting; where shaping input ("skip #2", "fold #1") goes; how open questions and tracker candidates get a disposition; where the label and routing reason appear; how many prompts the clean and approve-all paths take.
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the report → draft → post sequence before addressing Findings 8–12 individually

findings.title: Nothing records or shows whether a finding was executed or only re-read
findings.why_it_matters: D1-A ratifies that "depth relies on the skill's instructions". The design adds no way to tell a proved finding from one that was re-read and described as proved. The audit has the exact failure: the report said "independently confirmed by direct execution" when only a subagent had executed. D1's recommendation text also overstates the evidence. It says B is the only option not depending on "an instruction it skipped in 17 of 18 runs", but today's Phase 4 (SKILL.md:123-132) never asks for execution. The audit shows the skill didn't ask, not that sessions ignore the request. Sessions that were asked did dig (50558, 50163). So what A lacks is a trigger and a record, not capability.
findings.recommended: A: Each Medium+ finding in the report carries a required **Proof** line: the command run plus a one-line result, or `not run: <reason>`. The report may not say "verified/confirmed/proven" unless a command appears in that line.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Reviewers already produce runnable falsifiers, and the design never asks for or uses them
findings.why_it_matters: Reviewers have Bash and sometimes execute: in 50699 the code-reviewer ran `match_payer_pair` four ways. They also hand over runnable checks nobody runs: in 50886 the code-reviewer gave two read-only `dbx-api sql` falsifiers ("Zero means the claim in the docs holds") and the session ran neither. The design routes more context *to* reviewers (Phase 0) but leaves their dispatch prompt (SKILL.md:80-84) unchanged, so Phase 4 starts from nothing instead of from the reviewers' own checks.
findings.recommended: A: Add to the reviewer dispatch: for each finding, return the single command that would falsify it and, if it is read-only and cheap, its result. Phase 4 starts from those commands and re-runs them rather than inventing checks.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: The inline investigation has no bound, order, or progress signal, and no point where the user can prune it
findings.why_it_matters: The Posture assumes "a handful of findings". The audit's 50795 had 24. D4 sends every Medium+ finding, checkable claim, and own-thread finding through serial inline checks, D6 adds a target-branch check to each, and the Posture requires one command per Bash call. Nothing says when to stop, in what order to work, or what the user sees meanwhile. That can mean tens of silent minutes on large PRs, which are the PRs where wrong findings cost most. The user often has context that kills a finding instantly (50685: "every cluster will have event logs"; 50558: "Medium #2 can be skipped, as can Low #5"), and the design gives that context no place to enter before the work is spent. Long serial runs are also where a Sonnet session drifts back to re-reading (Finding 3).
findings.recommended: A: Before Phase 4, post a short non-blocking queue (severity, one-line gist, planned check per finding). Cap each finding at one decisive check, then settle it or route it to open questions. Print one status line per finding as it settles.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: The open-questions section can absorb checks the session could have run
findings.why_it_matters: D3 requires each open question to state "the one check that would settle it". If that check can be named, it can usually be run, which is the audit's complaint: "pushes onto the author a lineage check the reviewer could have run" (50907) and "handed the author the check the session could have run itself" (50163 #6). D3 moves that debt from the author to the user without removing it, against the user's stated "resolve questions before asking them" (50955) and "if we can confirm that its one less item to post" (50163). The section then looks diligent while listing things nobody ran.
findings.recommended: A: An item enters open questions only if its settling check cannot be run by the session (needs author intent, a credential it lacks, a system it can't reach) or the check errored or was denied. A runnable check that wasn't run is a defect to fix before reporting, not an open question.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Investigation progress isn't persisted, so a head move or a dead session loses completed proof
findings.why_it_matters: Today's Phase 4 step 1 redoes Phases 1–3 when the head moves. With a much longer Phase 4, an author push during investigation is more likely and throws away more work. Nothing is written as findings settle, so a compaction or crash mid-phase (50163 ran 2.5 h) leaves nothing to resume from. A written per-finding verdict would also be the evidence log behind Finding 3's Proof line.
findings.recommended: A: Write each finding's verdict (check, result, outcome) to the run's tmpdir as it settles. On a head move, re-check everything as today, using the log only as a reference.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Findings are shown twice, once in the report and again in full drafts
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 5 shows every finding with its bucket. The new Phase 6 rule shows full draft bodies on top of that, and D3/D6 add open questions and tracker candidates. One scroll then holds overview, findings, open questions, tracker candidates, and every full draft, followed by a three-option gate. The audit's "approved unseen" complaint is fixed by showing bodies once, not twice. In 50163 the user asked to open drafts in a browser because they were unreadable inline.
findings.recommended: C: Phase 5 shows thread-bound findings as one line each (severity, bucket, gist, proof status); full bodies appear once, in Phase 6.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: Open questions have no exit path in the gate
findings.why_it_matters: D3 says the user can "post it, dig, or drop it", but the Phase 7 gate's three options are all about drafts. Three things are undefined. "Dig" has no defined re-entry into Phase 4 or rule for what is re-shown. "Post it" has no template, since D5's Blocking/ask-first form assumes a proven claim and a question to the author is neither. And nothing says where each item is decided. Each session will invent its own handling.
findings.recommended: A: Give each open question a disposition in the same gate call (Dig / Post as question / Drop; default Drop below Medium). Dig re-enters Phase 4 for that item only and re-shows only the changed draft. Add a short author-question template to REFERENCE.md.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: No defined gate between the report and drafting, so shaping input costs a full redraft
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 5 flows straight into Phase 6. Sessions improvise a "draft them?" prompt the skill doesn't contain ("yeah go ahead and draft them", "Draft all 5"). The user's corrections cluster at this point: 50685 (script is being removed, fold #1 into a bullet), 50558 (skip #2/#5), 50163 (add a finding). Each currently costs a full draft-and-edit round trip, which full-body display makes longer.
findings.recommended: A: End the report with one gate: "Draft these threads" (default) / "Change the set first" / "Stop". Remove the improvised yes/no.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: The Blocking label is the session's call, and "touched pre-existing is Non-blocking" is fixed
findings.why_it_matters: D5's `[Blocking|Non-blocking]` label tells the author what blocks approval, which is the user's merge decision. The user repeatedly re-leveled findings after seeing them: 50303 ("worth fixing while you're in here"), 50558 (overrode a skip), and 50685 (downgraded to a bullet). A wrong label is the first thing the author reads. D5 also fixes "pre-existing issues the PR touches" as Non-blocking, which leaves no way to mark a serious touched item Blocking.
findings.recommended: A: Show each draft's label with a one-line reason as a first-class field, so "make #3 non-blocking" is a one-clause edit. Make "touched pre-existing → Non-blocking" the default rather than a fixed rule.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: D6's introduced/touched/pre-existing routing is decided silently per finding
findings.why_it_matters: D6 routes each finding by whether the PR "touches", "copies or extends", or leaves alone a target-branch issue. That is a judgment from a target-branch grep. The 50795 miss was this exact call made wrong: "master doesn't call it either" was read as not-our-problem while the PR caused the drift. If the routing isn't shown, the user can't catch a wrong demotion to tracker candidate.
findings.chosen: Add one bullet to D6's "Rule under A": "Each Medium+ finding shows its routing outcome (introduced / touched / copies-or-extends / pre-existing, untouched) and the one-line reason from the target-branch check, so a wrong demotion is visible and overridable."

findings.title: The head-SHA check can silently compare the Phase 1 fetch with itself
findings.why_it_matters: The design replaces the dead `lastMergeSourceCommit` read with `git ls-remote`. In 50795 the session fell back to `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`, which compares the Phase 1 fetch with itself and always passes. The Posture's "failed command is no answer" rule doesn't catch a comparison that succeeds but is stale.
findings.chosen: Extend the head-SHA bullet under "Mechanical fixes": "Compare a freshly `git ls-remote`'d SHA with the HEAD pinned in Phase 1; never substitute a local ref (`origin/<branch>`, `git rev-parse`), which compares the Phase 1 fetch to itself. If `ls-remote` fails (including a deleted source branch on a merged PR), the head check is 'no answer'."

findings.title: The clean-PR and no-finding fast paths aren't protected
findings.why_it_matters: Five of 12 audited runs were plain approvals. The design adds Phase 0 context gathering, a claims pass, and a per-finding target-branch check. It never says that today's "nothing survived → show overview, stop, no prompt" path (SKILL.md:140) survives the rewrite, and the Assumed section lists only the description check and the post gate as must-survive. D2 also makes "riskiest merge decision" a standing overview line, which forces a contrived sentence on a 20-line PR.
findings.chosen: Edit only the Summary, leaving D2 alone. In the "Context gathering" bullet, add "gathered in one batch, no per-item prompts". In the "Claims pass" bullet, add "the riskiest-merge-decision line is omitted when there is none". Add to Assumed bullet 5's must-survive list: "the stop-early path when nothing survives investigation (SKILL.md Phase 5: overview, 'no findings survived', no prompt)".

findings.title: The design doesn't say what the investigation may execute
findings.why_it_matters: "Executed evidence" means running a stranger's tests, scripts, or SQL under the user's credentials. The design never says what is allowed: read-only queries, PR-branch tests, writes to sandbox. The Rhyme "never run DML yourself" rule is loaded only on RHYME, and this skill also runs on GitHub repos. A permission denial also needs to be told apart from an error, or it lands in open questions as an unforced chore.
findings.recommended: A: Add to Phase 4: read-only commands and sandbox/scratch writes only; no DML against non-sandbox targets; PR-branch code runs only inside the review worktree; a denied command is reported as "blocked by permissions", distinct from "errored".
findings.chosen: A: Add to Phase 4: read-only commands and sandbox/scratch writes only; no DML against non-sandbox targets; PR-branch code runs only inside the review worktree; a denied command is reported as "blocked by permissions", distinct from "errored".

findings.title: Mechanical fixes work around `ado-api` output gaps instead of fixing the tool
findings.why_it_matters: `_pr_to_dict` returns only id, title, source, target, status, author, isDraft, creationDate, and description (analytics `packages/ado-api/src/ado_api/commands/pr.py:99-114`). The skill encodes `git ls-remote` as a second source of truth for the head commit and strips a header line from `ado-api pr threads`. Every other consumer of `ado-api` hits the same gaps. The design treats edits to other repos as out of scope, and D7 ratified "no follow-up" for an analytics edit, which is relevant here because `ado-api` lives in the analytics repo. Synthesis note: the same function also drops `lastMergeCommit`, which SKILL.md:41 (Phase 0 step 4) reads to find the pre-merge base for merged ADO PRs. The design's mechanical fixes don't cover that read, so the merged-PR path on ADO keeps reading a field the tool never returns, whichever side is chosen.
findings.chosen: Side B: Workaround + follow-up

findings.title: Findings converge on the head check and head-moved re-run path
findings.why_it_matters: Three findings from two critics land on one mechanism: the pinned-SHA head check in Phase 4 step 1 and the automatic re-run it triggers when the head moved. Finding 2 says it runs once, before the longest stretch of the skill. Finding 3 says the ADO lookup that feeds it is under-specified. Finding 13 says the re-run's cleanup clause deletes files on an inferred "these are mine". Each proposes a local patch. Together they ask whether the mechanism's shape (where the check sits, and whether a moved head triggers an automatic redo of Phases 0-3 or hands back to the user) should be re-evaluated rather than patched three times. Accepting the current shape and documenting its limits is also a valid outcome.
findings.recommended: B: Keep the mechanism and address Findings 2, 3, 13 individually.
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the head check and head-moved re-run before addressing Findings 2, 3, 13 individually.

findings.title: Head check runs once, before the longest phase; nothing re-checks before posting
findings.why_it_matters: Every posted thread cites file:line and command output from the pinned commit (REFERENCE.md:15-16). The only head comparison is at Phase 4 step 1, followed by the open-ended investigation, the shaping gate, drafting and the post gate. If the author pushes in that window, a thread lands under the user's name describing code that no longer exists: the "already fixed" false positive step 2 exists to prevent, and it can't be unsent (SKILL.md:236). Separately, "before resuming here" in step 1 doesn't say whether the re-run resumes at step 1 (re-checks) or step 2 (leaves the second window unchecked).
findings.recommended: A: Before the Phase 7 question, run the Phase 0 head command again; if the head moved, say so in the post-gate message (which SHA the drafts cite, that the author pushed since) and let the user decide, with no automatic redo. Also say the step 1 re-run resumes at step 1.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: ADO head check `git ls-remote origin '<source-branch>'` matches by ref suffix and has no meaning for empty output
findings.why_it_matters: `git ls-remote <remote> <pattern>` matches the tail of ref names, so `fix/a` also matches `refs/heads/foo/fix/a` and tags. A first-line match on the wrong ref gives a false "unchanged"; a mismatch gives a false "head moved" and the full Phase 0-3 redo. A branch deleted mid-review (Rhyme completes PRs with `--delete-source-branch`) returns exit 0 with empty output, which the "failed command" rule (SKILL.md:34) doesn't classify, so a session may compare "" to the pinned SHA and report "head moved". (Senior-engineer's further concern about a `refs/heads/` prefix on the ADO source name does not hold: `ado-api pr show --json` strips it.)
findings.chosen: In the Phase 0 table, change the ADO head-SHA cell to `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/<source-branch>'`. In Phase 4 step 1, add: "Use the line whose ref is exactly `refs/heads/<source-branch>`. Empty output means the branch is gone or renamed: report 'head check: no answer (branch not found)' and continue against the pinned HEAD; don't compare."

findings.title: The ADO CI command can never return the PR's validation builds
findings.why_it_matters: Workflow-ux flagged that an empty CI list from `ado-api builds list --branch 'refs/pull/<id>/merge'` has no stated meaning, since SKILL.md:58 only turns *errors* into "no answer". Verification shows it is worse: `ado-api` prepends `refs/heads/` to `--branch` (`builds.py:67-68`), so the query is for `refs/heads/refs/pull/<id>/merge` and returns an empty list on every ADO run. "Whether CI passed" is one of the four context items Phase 0 step 6 gathers for the reviewers and the investigation's "read the CI logs" check, and on ADO (the main use) it is silently always empty, liable to be written into context.md as "no CI" or read as nothing failing. The build call's reasoning (design.md:245, validation builds run on that ref) is right about ADO, but the tool can't express the query.
findings.recommended: A: Replace the ADO CI cell with a command verified against a real PR to return its validation builds (candidates: unfiltered `ado-api builds list --top <n> --json` matched on `sourceBranch == refs/pull/<id>/merge`, or `az pipelines runs list --branch 'refs/pull/<id>/merge'` via the AAD token route), and say an empty result is recorded as "no builds found on that ref", never as a pass.
findings.chosen: just tell it what to do/attempt to do, not how to to do - don't need any specific commands. i'll also always have az isntalled with the devops extension so thats also an option

findings.title: The `judgment:` route is an escape hatch the closing check accepts
findings.why_it_matters: The audit's root failure was sessions stopping at a re-read. `Evidence: judgment: <reasoning>` is a legal terminal state for any Medium+ finding, defined by the session's own conclusion that "no executable check applies" (SKILL.md:167), and the Phase 4 closing check (SKILL.md:182) is satisfied by writing the word. A High judgment finding still defaults to Blocking (design.md:248). SKILL.md:170 ("Re-reading the PR's own code is not a check") and the route point in opposite directions with no tie-break, and a finding where the reviewer named a command (SKILL.md:105-107) but the session wrote `judgment:` is contradictory with nothing to flag it. D1 accepted that depth rides on instruction strength (design.md:75), which makes this the weakest point. All three critics agree the route itself is needed.
findings.recommended: A: In step 5, add: "If a reviewer named a command, run it before anything else. `judgment:` is only for findings about naming, design shape, or prose; a finding about runtime behavior, consumers, or coverage is never judgment-only: run its check, or make it an open question."
findings.chosen: A: In step 5, add: "If a reviewer named a command, run it before anything else. `judgment:` is only for findings about naming, design shape, or prose; a finding about runtime behavior, consumers, or coverage is never judgment-only: run its check, or make it an open question."

findings.title: The Dropped list's scope is ambiguous, and it vanishes on the all-dropped stop path
findings.why_it_matters: The Dropped list exists so a wrong drop can be caught (SKILL.md:178). But the stop path at SKILL.md:194 ("show the overview, say nothing survived, and stop") reads as omitting it, exactly when every finding was dropped and a wrong drop is most likely. Its scope is also "refuted finding" only (SKILL.md:192), while findings are also dropped as thread duplicates, as already-said-in-the-description, and as resolved threads fixed at HEAD (SKILL.md:162), none of which have a refuting command. Sessions will either omit these or invent commands. Both critics note the build call's D3 justification (design.md:250) is off, since D3 covers unsettled findings, not refuted ones; the real justification (catching a wrong drop) holds.
findings.recommended: A: Item 5 lists every Medium+ finding removed in Phase 4 with its reason (the refuting command, "duplicate of thread <id>", "description already says it", "resolved thread <id>, fixed at HEAD"), and line 194 becomes "show the overview and the Dropped list, say nothing else survived, and stop."
findings.chosen: does that mean i'm going to need to read all of those? i trust opus to surface what matters and i'd rahter not read a whole list of dropped findings
findings.choice_reason: Applied as option C: Dropped list deleted

findings.title: Severity is never re-graded after the investigation, but labels and threading hang on it
findings.why_it_matters: Blocking/Non-blocking (REFERENCE.md:26-28) and whether a finding gets its own thread (SKILL.md:153) key off the reviewer's pre-proof severity. Phase 4 requires stating the impact (SKILL.md:167) but no step sets severity from it. A High the investigation shrinks to cosmetic stays Blocking; a Medium proven to break a consumer stays Non-blocking. The audit's wrong-HIGH cases (50558, 50534, 50303) had this shape.
findings.chosen: In Phase 4 step 5, add: "Set each surviving finding's severity from the impact the investigation proved, not the reviewer's estimate. A finding that falls below Medium folds or drops like any Low."

findings.title: Tests and docs bucket findings below Medium get a posted thread on a re-read alone
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 3 buckets every finding first; only code issues are gated at Medium+ for their own thread (SKILL.md:153). Phase 6 drafts the tests and docs buckets unconditionally (SKILL.md:216), while Phase 4 investigates only Medium+ (SKILL.md:167, 171). So a Low test-gap finding is posted in its own thread backed by a re-read, though the template demands "the evidence actually run" (REFERENCE.md:15-16) and the worked example's point is that a grep proved the gap (REFERENCE.md:59). D4 is ambiguous here (design.md:116). A tests claim is the cheapest kind to prove.
findings.recommended: A: In step 4, include every tests and docs bucket finding regardless of severity (one grep or consumer check each).
findings.chosen: C: Leave as is.

findings.title: Tracker candidates are proven only by existing at `<base>`
findings.why_it_matters: The build call says "showing it exists at `<base>` is enough proof" and skips step 4 (SKILL.md:166; design.md:247). That proves two things less than the report implies. (1) Existence at `<base>` proves the code is old, not that the reviewer's claim about its effect is true: the audit's re-read failure rerouted to a different destination (structural-minimalist). (2) `<base>` is the merge-base, right for "would this exist without the PR" but not for "is this worth filing": on a stale branch the issue may already be fixed at `origin/<target>`'s tip (senior-engineer). Audience assumption: repos where branches go stale for days; the Rhyme rules treat two-week-stale branches as normal. The report lists the candidate with no marker that either is unchecked, and the user is invited to file it.
findings.recommended: A: For each tracker candidate, add one `git grep '<pattern>' 'origin/<target>'` and report "still present at target tip" or "already fixed on target"; label candidates in Phase 5 item 4 "exists at `<base>`; effect not checked".
findings.chosen: D: Delete the "enough proof, skip step 4" clause

findings.title: "Draft a tracker candidate" and replies after an early stop have no defined continuation
findings.why_it_matters: SKILL.md:212 lets the user "draft a tracker candidate", but Phase 6 drafts only PR threads (SKILL.md:216), REFERENCE.md has no tracker shape, and Phase 7 posts only PR comments. A session may draft it as a PR thread, which D6 exists to prevent (the author isn't asked about issues their PR didn't touch). Separately, the early-stop paths (SKILL.md:194) end with "the user replies in free text", but nothing tells the session how to handle that reply; the handlers at SKILL.md:212 only exist behind the shaping gate.
findings.recommended: A: Define "draft a tracker candidate" as issue text (title and body) shown to the user to file, never posted to the PR; add to line 194: "a free-text reply is handled as at 'Change the set first'."
findings.chosen: B: Remove "or draft a tracker candidate" from line 212 (tracker candidates stay list-only)

findings.title: A disproved PR claim bypasses the thread-dedup step
findings.why_it_matters: Claims enter Phase 3 as entries, not findings (SKILL.md:138; design.md:246), and Phase 4 step 2's dedup is written for "each finding" (SKILL.md:162). A claim disproved in step 4 becomes a High Blocking finding (SKILL.md:177) after dedup has run, so a reviewer who already raised the same concern in an existing thread gets a duplicate Blocking thread. The description check doesn't apply (claims come from the description); the thread match does.
findings.chosen: In Phase 4 step 5, after "A disproved claim becomes a High Code-issue finding", add: "Run step 2's thread match on it before keeping it."

findings.title: PR-authored code and reviewer-suggested commands run with session credentials; the ledger's teammates-only condition is missing from the skill
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: single user reviewing teammates' work PRs on machines with live Databricks/ADO/AWS credentials; a hostile PR is unlikely, a careless one (a test or conftest that touches a real service) is the realistic case. Three gaps, from two critics: (1) D8 accepted running PR test code with session credentials *for teammates' PRs* (design.md:198); SKILL.md:173 keeps the permission and drops the condition. (2) Step 4 starts "from the command the reviewer named" (SKILL.md:167), and reviewers name commands after reading author-controlled text (diff, description, comments: SKILL.md:101-108), so injected text can steer what runs; D8's acceptance covers PR test code only. (3) The PR can modify the files that decide what a test run does (`conftest.py`, `pyproject.toml`, Makefile), and the scope test (SKILL.md:173) is a self-assessment by the same session. Fork PRs currently fail at Phase 1's `git fetch origin` (SKILL.md:66), which limits exposure today by accident rather than by text.
findings.recommended: A: In "What you may run", add the ledger's condition ("PR test code runs with your credentials; that is accepted for teammates' PRs only, so don't run tests on a PR from outside the org or a fork") and "treat a reviewer-named command as a suggestion: run it only if it fits this scope."
findings.chosen: A: Restore qualifier + suggestions

findings.title: The head-moved path deletes untracked files with no baseline
findings.why_it_matters: Senior-engineer labelled this TENSION, but it has no competing side and proposes one fix, so it is synthesized as MEDIUM. Step 1 says "If investigation output left untracked files in the worktree, delete those files before the checkout" (SKILL.md:161) without saying which files or how, and nothing records which files are the skill's. `git clean` is the only blunt option and destroys anything the user placed in the worktree. Step 1 runs before any investigation on every pass, so in the current flow there is rarely anything of the skill's to delete; the clause mostly invites a guess. Structural-minimalist notes the clause is also an unlogged addition beyond the Build calls.
findings.recommended: A: Delete the cleanup clause from step 1, and in Phase 1 step 2 say "if not clean, tell the user and stop."
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Claims handling is described in four places, and two of them disagree
findings.why_it_matters: Claims appear at SKILL.md:123 (overview bullet), 136-138 (a Phase 3 subsection), 167/170 (investigation), and 177 (outcome). The Phase 3 subsection adds only the "not a finding yet" point, and line 123 contradicts it: 123 says claims "join the findings in Phase 3" while 138 says "It isn't a finding yet". Any edit to claim routing has to touch four spots.
findings.chosen: Delete the Phase 3 "Add the PR's claims" subsection (SKILL.md:136-138). In line 123, replace "These join the findings in Phase 3 and get proved or disproved in Phase 4" with "Each one is an entry for Phase 4 to prove or disprove, not a finding: a confirmed claim is noted in the overview, a disproved one becomes a High Code-issue finding."

findings.title: The riskiest-merge-decision line is written in Phase 2 and then rewritten in Phase 5
findings.why_it_matters: The overview is first shown in the Phase 5 report. The riskiest-decision line is drafted in Phase 2 before any check runs (SKILL.md:124), then "re-derived" in Phase 5 (SKILL.md:188), and nothing in Phase 4 uses the Phase 2 draft. It is written twice, the first version always discarded, with a stale-line risk if the re-derive is skipped. Senior-engineer and workflow-ux judged the re-derive build call sound as written; structural-minimalist argues writing it once is the better fix. D2 placed the line in the overview (design.md:89), which is where the user reads it either way.
findings.recommended: A: Remove the "Riskiest merge decision" bullet from Phase 2 and make Phase 5 item 1 say "add the riskiest merge decision and what you recommend, from what Phase 4 proved; omit it when there is none."
findings.chosen: A: Remove the "Riskiest merge decision" bullet from Phase 2 and make Phase 5 item 1 add it from what Phase 4 proved

findings.title: The "re-reading is not proof" rationale is stated three times
findings.why_it_matters: The rationale appears in SKILL.md:9, the Phase 4 opener (157-159), line 170, and REFERENCE.md:63-65. Nothing in SKILL.md points to the REFERENCE section, and the session reads REFERENCE.md for the template in Phase 6, after Phase 4 is done, so that copy arrives too late to steer anything. D8 asked to keep the skill small (design.md:184); the REFERENCE section itself was ratified to exist (design.md:30).
findings.recommended: A: Delete REFERENCE.md:63-65; keep the Phase 4 opener.
findings.chosen: B: Delete REFERENCE.md:63-65 and trim the Phase 4 opener to its last paragraph (line 159).

findings.title: The pre-report self-check restates step 5
findings.why_it_matters: SKILL.md:182 ("go through the Medium-and-above findings and claims once more: each has a command on its Evidence line, a `judgment:` line, or a place in the open questions") repeats the rules at 175 and 180, a third statement of one rule. Workflow-ux reads the same line as the phase's closing guard (and the one Finding 5's escape hatch satisfies), so critics differ on whether it is redundancy or a needed gate.
findings.recommended: B: Keep it.

findings.title: "Compact report, read once" versus the full Evidence line in every report entry
findings.why_it_matters: D9's rationale is that each thing is read once (design.md:208). Step 5 requires the Evidence line to quote "the command run and the part of its output that settles the finding" (SKILL.md:175), the report puts that line in every entry (SKILL.md:189), and the drafts restate the same evidence in their "why" (REFERENCE.md:15-16). On a large PR the report stops being one line per finding, and the severity/label/routing signal the shaping gate acts on gets buried. But D9 also ratified the Evidence line in the report (design.md:219), and it's what lets the user catch an overclaim before drafting.
findings.chosen: Side B: Cap report Evidence
